name: Microsoft_AD_GroupManagement_Events
description: Active Directory security-group events (16 Security log event IDs) from domain controllers.
technicalNotes:
Ingests the Active Directory group-management events from each domain controller's Security log into LM Logs: security groups (global, local, universal) created, changed, deleted, and members added or removed, and a group's type or scope changed. Distribution groups are left out: they grant no permissions.

AppliesTo ships empty, so the module collects nothing until you set it. To collect from every domain controller, set it to: hasCategory("MicrosoftDomainController")

Prerequisites:
- Advanced audit policy on the domain controllers: Account Management > Audit Security Group Management, Success (Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Advanced Audit Policy Configuration). Check the effective setting on a DC with: auditpol /get /category:"Account Management". With auditing off no events are written, and this module has nothing to ingest. A check that alerts when it is off is planned as a separate module.
- LM reads the events over WMI (Win32_NTLogEvent) as the Collector's service account, or as wmi.user/wmi.pass when set. That account needs read access to the Security log (Manage auditing and security log, SeSecurityPrivilege).

Every event this module ingests carries ad_event_category=group_management, so one LM Logs query finds them all.

The core Windows Event Logs LogSource excludes Security Audit Success events, so running both does not ingest these events twice, unless that exclusion has been removed.

If no events arrive: check the lmlogs.winevent.channels property first, then the audit policy, then the account's Security-log access.
